mechanism_narrative: A 2% quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strengthening economic growth, leading to increased consumer spending and, subsequently, higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of quarters with 2%+ GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle, increasing borrowing costs and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly lower (t-test p < 0.05) in periods with FEDFUNDS > 5% compared to baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Jointly, when UNRATE falls below 4% and PAYEMS increases by 0.5% in a month, it indicates a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: Rank IC for this joint condition remains below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 1.5% monthly increase in INDPRO signals increased industrial production, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not positively correlated (Pearson's r > 0.1) with INDPRO growth over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) increases by 1% in a month, it indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward analysis shows no significant positive return (t-test p > 0.05) following the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: The spread between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation rate) narrowing to less than 2% indicates a balanced monetary policy, leading to stable S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX volatility (20-day std dev) remains high (> 15%) during periods with a narrow spread.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in UNRATE by 0.5% in two months, without a corresponding increase in PAYEMS, may signal labor market inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decrease > 0.5% in 2 months, with PAYEMS unchanged
failure_condition: Rank IC for this condition does not predict negative returns (IC < 0.01) over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in HOUST (housing starts) by 5% in a month indicates a strong housing market, boosting economic growth and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not significantly higher (t-test p < 0.05) following a 5% increase in HOUST compared to baseline.
